entities.summary:
Gongmin, also known as Bayan Temür, was 31st ruler of Goryeo from 1351 to 1374. He was the second son of King Chungsuk.

Born into a powerful royal family, Gongmin ascended to the throne after the death of his older brother and half-brother. His reign was marked by internal power struggles, regional conflicts, and the ongoing Mongol-led Yuan dynasty's efforts to maintain control over Korea.

Despite these challenges, Gongmin implemented various policies aimed at strengthening Goryeo's economy and military, including the establishment of new trade routes and the recruitment of additional soldiers. He also continued his father's efforts to promote Buddhism and the arts.

Gongmin's legacy is complex, with some historians viewing him as a capable and just ruler who effectively managed the kingdom's internal affairs, while others see him as ineffective and powerless in the face of external pressures.

The reign of Gongmin marked the final years of the Goryeo dynasty, which would eventually fall to the Joseon dynasty in 1392, more than 18 years after his death.

Gongmin's life and reign remain a topic of interest among historians, with many focusing on the intricacies of Goryeo's politics, economy, and culture during this period.
